key_insight: SyncLight is the first method that enables controllable, parametric relighting that remains photometrically consistent across multiple uncalibrated views of a static scene, allowing precise control of light intensity and color while preserving cross-view coherence.
problem_solved: Existing single-view generative relighting methods fail to guarantee rigorous lighting consistency across multiple cameras, which prevents their use in multi-camera broadcasts, stereoscopic cinema, and virtual production pipelines; SyncLight addresses this gap.
method: Accepts uncalibrated multi-view images and explicit lighting parameters (intensity, color) as input and produces relit images for each view with shared lighting behavior.

Learns a joint multi-view representation and enforces cross-view photometric consistency via multi-view consistency losses during training, ensuring coherent shadows, highlights, and color across views.
Provides controllable, parametric edits (e.g., sliders for intensity and hue) so users can precisely and consistently manipulate scene illumination across all cameras.
impact: Enables practitioners to perform photorealistic, controllable relighting across multi-camera captures—facilitating virtual production, stereoscopic content, and any pipeline that requires consistent multi-view lighting. It bridges single-view relighting advances with production-grade multi-view requirements.
visual_elements: Before/after multi-view grid: several camera views showing original vs. SyncLight-relit outputs with matched lighting
Pipeline diagram: inputs (multi-view images + lighting parameters) → SyncLight model → consistent per-view outputs, annotated with consistency loss

Control UI mockup: icons for intensity slider and color wheel showing how the same controls affect all views
paper_title: SyncLight: Controllable and Consistent Multi-View Relighting
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Anand Bhattad, Luis Herranz, Jean-François Lalonde, Javier Vazquez-Corral
